paper.title: Trust the Batch, On- or Off-Policy: Adaptive Policy Optimization for RL Post-Training
paper.authors: Rasool Fakoor, Murdock Aubry, Nicholas Stranges, Alexander J. Smola
paper.central_question: Can the current batch quantify behavior-policy mismatch and set both policy-gradient weighting and off-policy regularization without a fixed clipping factor?

section_policy.sequence_rule: Begin with the paper's motivating question, establish the prior objective and terminology before the mechanism, connect the mechanism to original code, then separate experimental evidence from limitations.

sections.title: Introduction (pages 1-2; page 1 not in image set)
claims: Two concerns underlie RL fragility: a trust-region concern (each update should not move the policy far from its current value) and an off-policy concern (data from older or different behavior policies should influence the update only to the extent it remains reliable).

Off-policy data arise from optimizer steps reused across iterations, rollouts from older or heterogeneous policies, and rollout/training engine mismatches in numerical precision, sampling strategy or architecture.

Current methods conflate the two concerns inside a single fixed-clip mechanism; decoupled-loss methods and asymmetric/sequence-level clips re-parameterize the clip but leave the amount of trust as an external choice.

Premise: fixed clipping itself, not the clip value, causes the fragility; the batch's ESS over per-token importance ratios measures how on-policy the batch is and drives both the score-function cap and the regularizer.
Contribution: adopt the P3O objective of Fakoor et al. [7] for large-model post-training (first such application); no new hyper-parameter; handles on- and off-policy data in one objective.

sections.title: Background (Eqs. 1-8)
claims: Token-level MDP: state s_t = (x, y_<t), action y_t, scalar terminal reward r(x,y); REINFORCE estimator Eq. 2 is on-policy and high-variance; a baseline b gives advantage A = r - b.
Group-relative advantage (GRPO, Eq. 3): per-prompt mean and population std over G completions replace the value function.
PPO (Eq. 4) clips the per-token ratio rho_t against a fresh snapshot pi_old with range [1-eps_l, 1+eps_h] fixed before training.
Off-policy data: importance sampling (Eqs. 5-6) restores unbiasedness by reweighting with pi_theta/pi_b; the per-token ratio Eq. 7 generalizes the PPO-snapshot ratio to any behavior policy.
Remark: ratios are bounded below by zero and unbounded above, so a few unlikely-under-pi_b tokens can dominate the gradient; the standard remedy is clipping.
RL in LM: the objective adds a KL penalty eta * KL(pi_theta || pi_theta_0) toward a frozen reference (Eq. 8).

sections.title: Approach (Eqs. 9-12, Table 1)
claims: Per-token contribution of Eq. 4 by sign of A: for A>0 it is -min(ratio, 1+eps_h)A (ceiling once ratio > 1+eps_h); for A<0 it is -max(ratio, 1-eps_l)A (floor once ratio < 1-eps_l); beyond the band the token gives no further credit (zero gradient).

When the batch is fresh rho_t ~ 1 and the clip is rarely active; when stale or from a different policy, (eps_l, eps_h) decides what fraction of the batch contributes; too small clips many tokens, too large admits high-variance gradients; no single value suits both regimes.
Prior work re-parameterizes the clip but does not remove it: GRPO symmetric eps, DAPO asymmetric, GSPO sequence-level geometric mean with its own eps^seq.

ESS of the policy ratios in the current batch (Eq. 11) lies in [1/|B|, 1]; e_B = sg(ESS) is treated as a constant for backpropagation; ESS is near one when ratios are nearly uniform and falls when a few large ratios dominate.
P3O (Eq. 12) replaces the fixed clip with two terms whose strength is set by e_B: the score-function weight min{rho_t, e_B} (stop-gradient) and the regularizer (1 - e_B) KL(pi_theta || pi_old).

Unlike the clip in Eq. 4, which discards the gradient of every token outside the band, min{rho_t, e_B} only scales the score-function gradient by a positive factor: every token contributes and no data is wasted; Eq. 12 introduces no clipping range, trust-region coefficient or staleness budget.
Table 1 contrasts GRPO/DAPO, GSPO, Decoupled (prox snapshot, outer behavior weight cap c_w) and P3O, colouring fixed hyper-parameters vs batch-adaptive quantities.

Off-policy data in large-model training: the decoupled-loss fix (clip against pi_prox) adds the construction of pi_prox, its lifetime and the cap c_w; P3O's e_B falls when the batch becomes off-policy so one objective covers both regimes.

sections.title: A potential issue with P3O (Eq. 13)
claims: A single e_B conflates two drifts: pi_theta vs the data-generating pi_b, and pi_theta vs its pre-update snapshot pi_prox; when both are large in different directions a single anchor cannot distinguish them.

Extension Eq. 13: second anchor at pi_prox, joint ESS e_mix, mixture pi_mix of pi_b and pi_prox weighted by (1-e_b) and (1-e_prox); reduces to P3O when either anchor is uninformative; no new hyper-parameter.
Empirically the single-anchor P3O matches or slightly outperforms this variant across the regimes in Sec. 4 (appendix D: the two-anchor variant is unstable at T=1.2, not verified from page images).

sections.title: Experiments (§4.1-4.4, Figs. 1-4, Tables 3-7)
claims: Three axes: (i) sensitivity to the clip hyper-parameters P3O eliminates; (ii) robustness to off-policy data from numerical precision and sampling temperature; (iii) held-out math benchmarks. Baseline is GRPO with identical hyper-parameters otherwise (Table 3).

§4.1 Setup: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Qwen2.5-1.5B on DeepScaleR-Preview (40,000 problem-answer pairs from AIME 1984-2023, AMC pre-2023, Omni-MATH, Still); binary rewards, no shaping; 8 H100 GPUs with optimizer workers separated from rollout engines.

§4.2 Clipping factor: symmetric eps in {0.2, 0.4, 0.6} for GRPO vs a single P3O run; Fig. 1 shades +-1 std over clip values (not seeds); GRPO's trajectory varies with eps, P3O stays stable; DAPO/GSPO show the same sensitivity so the isolated variable is presence vs absence of a fixed clip.

§4.3 Temperature: T != 1 shifts per-token log-probabilities; Fig. 2 on Qwen3-4B at T=0.6 and T=1.2: GRPO degrades at both, collapsing at T=1.2 after ~step 20 while P3O stays ~0.6; Qwen2.5-1.5B deferred to Fig. 7.
§4.3 BF16 train + FP8 rollout at 16,384 max tokens: Fig. 3(a) Qwen3-4B GRPO falls from ~0.5 to ~0 after step ~20 while P3O stays ~0.5; Fig. 3(b) Qwen2.5-1.5B the two curves overlap around 0.2-0.28.

§4.4 Benchmarks: Fig. 4 pass@k averaged over AIME24/25/26, AMO-Bench, AMC; (a) clip variants at 4K-token eval, GRPO averaged over eps; (b) FP8 at 16K-token eval, GRPO near-zero by iter 30 while P3O retains performance; full numbers in Table 7 (appendix, not in image set).

sections.title: Discussion
claims: Trust placed in an update should be adaptive rather than pre-committed; P3O does not make arbitrary off-policy data reliable (meaningful token-level ratios and adequate support in the behavior data are still required) but turns mismatch into a measured batch property and removes clip ranges, behavior-weight caps and staleness budgets.

findings.question: Does performance depend on choosing a clipping factor?
findings.setting: GRPO with ε ∈ {0.2, 0.4, 0.6} versus one P3O objective
findings.takeaway: The paper reports sensitivity across fixed clip choices while P3O does not require a clip-ratio choice.

findings.question: How does sampling-temperature mismatch affect training?
findings.setting: Qwen3-4B with rollout temperature T=0.6 versus T=1.2
findings.takeaway: The paper reports P3O remains robust while GRPO degrades at the larger mismatch.

findings.question: Does train–rollout precision mismatch cause late collapse?
findings.setting: BF16 Train + FP8 Rollout at iterations 15 and 30
findings.takeaway: Table 7 reports GRPO falling from 0.499 to 0.029 while P3O changes from 0.478 to 0.529.

findings.question: Does the two-anchor extension remain stable under temperature mismatch?
findings.takeaway: The appendix reports the extension can be stable at default temperature but becomes unstable at T=1.2, preserving an important claim boundary.
